crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Evidence Extraction Tables
children.blurb: Evidence extraction tables are structured grids that turn the prose of studies into comparable rows and columns.

children.name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
children.blurb: Weighing the scientific consensus means assessing how much agreement exists across a body of research on a given question, rather than relying on a single study or a headline.

children.name: Questioning Your Own Sources
children.blurb: Questioning your own sources is the habit of auditing the evidence base of a review you are writing or have already published, rather than trusting the citations you have accumulated.

children.name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
children.blurb: Deep research agents and landscape scans cover the use of autonomous or semi-autonomous software to plan, run and report on broad literature searches.

children.name: Translating Between Disciplines
children.blurb: Translating between disciplines means taking findings, methods, or terminology from one research field and restating them so they can be used in another.

sections.body: Literature review and evidence synthesis is the work of turning many papers into a defensible account of what is known. AI systems now read full texts, pull out claims, populations, methods, outcomes, and limitations, and place them into structured tables. They cluster findings by topic, flag contradictions, and draft summaries that link back to the original paper. Deep research agents can run broad scans across fields, then narrow to a question. The aim is not to replace reading but to make a large body of work navigable and auditable. This section covers the methods and the cautions that come with them.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are genuinely useful now. Extraction of clear statements from open access papers works well enough to build large claim sets, and the site's library holds 135 research papers with 12,646 claims extracted from research works. Consensus is harder, because agreement is not a simple count and depends on study quality, effect sizes, and publication bias. Questioning your own sources is harder still, since models can miss retractions, conflicts, or methods that do not support the abstract. Cross disciplinary translation remains mostly a human task, with AI offering candidate bridges that need expert checking. The honest limit is that synthesis is not solved, and a fluent summary can still be wrong.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here form a sequence from raw evidence to wider interpretation, and a reader would go to each for a different stage of the review. Evidence Extraction Tables covers the mechanics of pulling claims into rows and columns, which is the base layer for everything else. Weighing the Scientific Consensus deals with how to judge agreement across studies without reducing it to a vote. Questioning Your Own Sources asks where the evidence came from, what it omits, and how to check it against the original paper. Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans covers broad, automated searches that map a field before a narrow review begins. Translating Between Disciplines addresses the movement of methods and findings across fields, where vocabulary and standards often differ.
